units.translation: O you who have been much hated, you who have subdued by force.
objects of hatred to the chaste.
objects of hatred to men and to the Olympian gods.
the tongue of a hateful dog.
and he prays that he will put the wages of my (i.e. of my bringing, which follows in v. 1263) in his wrath (Auratus: in his drink, Scaliger: in a vessel).
Now you judge for me exile from the city and the hatred of the citizens.
and you will be cityless, a mighty hatred to the citizens.

Mitrogathes, a Persian proper name, Pers. 43, first syllable long, penultimate short, where in M μητρογαθής: but comparison of similar Persian names (such as Μιτραδάτης and Μιτροβάτης in Herodotus) shows that the reading of the copies Μιτρογαθής is correct, except that with corrected accent it should be written Μιτρογάθης.
a memorial of your journey for all mortals.
Of a tomb in the epigram on Aeschylus (fr. 450): this tomb hides Aeschylus, who has perished.
and they crowned with their hands memorials of themselves for their parents in their homes, at the chariot of Adrastus.
and the combinations of letters, the mother of the Muses, the worker of memory (thus Hemsterhuis for μνήμην) of all things.
he once found a memory as a recompense in his prayers.
and he does not remember my commands.
which you write on the mindful tablets of your mind.
and august ones mindful of evils.
a mindful (thus Hermann for ἥμενον) thought from above somehow from there accomplished (Zeus) entirely from his holy seats.
remembering sorrows, born from the memory of sorrows
remembering sorrows, born from the memory of sorrows
to bring forth, to give birth
and you met with a bitter suitor for your marriage, O maiden.
and be mindful for me of the city's rites that love sacrifice.
share the toil with him who now toils.
and who of the unfortunate ones, alas, such as I, are toiling?
do not kick against the goads, lest you stumble and suffer.
where on earth have I, wretched one, wandered?
the wretched and unfortunate ones – the war-leaders.
Fate, giver of heavy gifts, wretched one.
self-born before birth, a wretched hare to those sacrificing.
οὐ μόλις not scarcely, but immediately.
